Questions.QuestionText: What is the scientific name of the Emperor Penguin?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Emperor Penguin (Aptenodytes forsteri) is the tallest and heaviest of all living penguin species and is endemic to Antarctica. The other answers were the Wandering Albatross (Diomedea exulans), the Common Wood Pigeon (Columba palumbus) and the Chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus)

Questions.QuestionText: What type of goose is pictured here?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Canada Goose is a large goose, with a distinctive black head and neck, and large white throat patch. A species originally from North America, it has successfully spread to cover most of the UK. The Grass Goose does not exist, but Goosegrass is a common name for several types of grasses, sedges and annual herbs (including Sticky Weed).

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following birds has the largest recorded wingspan?
Questions.AnswerFact: The largest recorded wingspan for the Wandering Albatross is 3.7m (12ft 2in). By comparison, the Great White Pelican reaches 3.6m (11ft 10in), the Andean Condor 3.3m (10ft 10in), and the Marabou Stork 3.2m (10ft 6in).

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following birds is poisonous?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Hooded Pitohui is a species of bird found in New Guinea, and one of the few known poisonous birds. Its skin and feathers contain batrachotoxin, the same potent neurotoxin found in Poison Dart Frogs. Scientists believe the toxin comes from beetles in its diet.

Questions.QuestionText: How many recognised species of wild pigeons and doves are there?
Questions.AnswerFact: The International Ornithological Committee recognises 352 in the Columbidae family (pigeons and doves), including around 13 extinct ones.

Questions.QuestionText: What type of bustard is pictured here?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Great Bustard (Otis tarda) is a bird in the bustard family, and one of the heaviest flying birds in the world. While Josie's Bustard is fictional, several real species are named after people, such as Ludwig's Bustard and Denham's Bustard.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following parrots is the heaviest on average?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Kākāpō is a large, green, flightless parrot and is the world's heaviest parrot, reaching weights of up to 4kg (8.8lbs). It is critically endangered and native to New Zealand.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the national bird of Saint Kitts and Nevis?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Brown Pelican, the smallest of the eight pelican species, is the national bird of Saint Kitts and Nevis. The other answers are the national birds of Nigeria (Black Crowned Crane), South Africa (Blue Crane), and Japan (Green Pheasant).

Questions.QuestionText: What can the colour of a chicken's earlobe typically indicate?
Questions.AnswerD: The colour that their eggs will be
Questions.AnswerFact: Earlobe colour is a good indicator of egg colour in many chicken breeds, but it isn't a definitive factor as some breeds are exceptions. Chickens with white earlobes usually lay white eggs, while those with red earlobes typically lay brown eggs.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the fastest bird in the world?
Questions.AnswerFact: The Peregrine Falcon is not only the fastest bird in the world, but is also the fastest animal in general. It can reach diving speeds over 200mph (320km/h), with a maximum recorded speed of 240mph (386km/h). If excluding diving speed, the White-throated Needletail is the fastest in level flight at 105mph (169km/h).

Questions.QuestionText: What is the common name of the bird 'Balaeniceps Rex'?
Questions.AnswerFact: Balaeniceps Rex is the scientific name of the Shoebill. The name means 'king whale-head', referring to its massive shoe-shaped bill.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following facts about the Hoatzin is true?
Questions.AnswerB: It has a unique digestive system
Questions.AnswerC: It has nostrils at the tip of its bill
Questions.AnswerFact: The Hoatzin has a unique foregut that ferments leaves, a digestive system similar to a cow. Because of this, it is often called the 'Stinkbird' due to its distinct, manure-like odor.
